thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed in eu-west-2 ingress pool (ing-proxy-eu-west-2). Alert triggered 10:12:08 UTC — 5xx rate ~9% over 3m, p95 latency spiking. Paging Maya (SRE) and Alex (Infra). Runbook: https://go/ops/runbooks/ingress-5xx (automated)
Maya: acked — I'm on it. Pulling logs, enabling full debug on the gateway. Can someone grab a quick customer-impact count? :eyes:
Lucy: Support report: 18 customer tickets opened so far, several high-priority customers reporting 502s. CS page opened: https://go/cs/incidents/3798642011
Alex: Looking at infra metrics — connection queue on the ingress proxy is saturating, backend pool reporting long socket wait times. Not seeing full node OOMs. Possible connection churn or upstream timeouts.
Rahul: Observed a sharp rise in backend connection resets around 10:11:40 UTC. Also an increase in redis KV cache miss latency in the same AZ (~ eu-west-2a). Could be cascading: cache miss -> backend surge -> proxy queue blowout.
Maya: grabbing live logs. Sample errors:
```
[10:11:42] gateway: upstream 10.12.34.56:443 error: connect() failed: Too many open files
[10:11:44] gateway: 502 from backend svc-runtime (req_id=abc123)
```
Maya: that "Too many open files" looks like FD exhaustion on proxy workers.
Alex: checking node ulimit and nginx worker_rlimit. Current rlimits = 1024 on several proxy VMs. That's low for our traffic profile. Why didn't autoscaling absorb? Pools were at ~85% CPU but not over scale threshold.
deploy-bot: Automated routing fallback attempted at 10:14:20 UTC -> failed (no healthy alternative pool in eu-west-1 tagged for that customer tier).
Maya: plan: 1) temporarily steer a fraction of traffic away from eu-west-2 to eu-west-1 (soft reroute) to buy time; 2) increase FD limit & restart proxy worker on two affected nodes; 3) drain one saturated proxy and scale extra instance if needed.
Alex: I can run soft-reroute. Command (control plane API):
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/v1/reroute \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"from":"ing-proxy-eu-west-2","to":"ing-proxy-eu-west-1","pct":20,"reason":"emergency backpressure"}'
```
Alex: issuing now. Response: 202 accepted. Routing change propagating (~30s).
Maya: starting FD bump on nodes proxy-eu2-04 and proxy-eu2-05. Steps:
```
sudo sysctl -w fs.file-max=200000
sudo bash -c 'echo "* soft nofile 200000\n* hard nofile 200000" >> /etc/security/limits.conf'
systemctl restart gateway-proxy
```
Rahul: while that happens, I'm increasing backend circuit-breaker threshold for svc-runtime in eu-west-2 to reduce retries causing head-of-line blocking.
Lucy: Notifying customers: standard incident message posted to status page and customer update channel. ETA for interim mitigation 15m.
Maya: FD bump succeeded on proxy-eu2-04, logs show backlog draining. proxy-eu2-05 still restarting (hung on a stale connection close, forcing restart now).
Alex: reroute at 20% reduced 5xx rate to ~5% in next minute. Good signal.
Rahul: backend circuit-breaker adjustment in place. Also toggled prefork worker scaling on runtime-service to +2 replicas in eu-west-2.
Maya: after restarts and reroute, current 5xx rate down to 1.6% and p95 latency back to baseline. Rolling removal of one saturated node from rotation.
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial) at 10:35:11 UTC. Customer-impact still present but contained; will monitor for 30m.
Lucy: posting customer update: "We identified transient connection limit exhaustion on the ingress proxy in eu-west-2, immediate mitigations are in place and requests are recovering. We are investigating root cause and will follow up."
Maya: action items for follow-up (assigning):
- Rahul: full postmortem + timeline + root cause hypotheses (redis miss pattern vs connection churn) — owner
- Alex: infra remediation: ensure rlimits baked into golden AMIs, add autoscale policy tweak to account for queue saturation (runbook update)
- Maya: add an automated guard in routing service to allow emergency soft-failover for customer tiers when local pool FD exhaustion detected
- Lucy: finalize customer communications and post-incident message on status page
Rahul: I'll own the postmortem. Initial hypothesis: a sudden cache eviction storm caused by a bad config rollout in svc-runtime in eu-west-2a leading to bursty backend load, exhausting proxy FDs. Will correlate deploy history and cache eviction logs.
Maya: handing off to Alex for overnight watch. I'm logging out in ~20m. Oncall handover: Alex is primary, Rahul is secondary.
oncall-rotation-bot: Next oncall (primary): Alex — pager rules unchanged. Runbook link posted.
Maya: closing thread for now. If we see >3% 5xx again, re-open and escalate to EngSig.
Alex: noted. Thanks all — will coordinate patch and postmortem comments tomorrow. :thumbsup:
